uncited: - **Output:** A global 3D Gaussian model (positions, covariances, opacities, SH coefficients) merged from local node states.
The system partitions the scene spatially.
Each node maintains a local subset of Gaussians.
- **Local Gaussians:** A subset of the global Gaussian set, defined by spatial bounds.
**Partition Dataset:** The training dataset (images and poses) is partitioned across nodes.
**Ghost Cell Management:** At the boundaries of each node's spatial partition, ghost cells are created.
Load a batch of images (camera views) assigned to this node.
Compute loss (L1 + SSIM) against ground truth images.
Update local Gaussian parameters (positions, covariances, SH coefficients, opacities) using Adam optimizer.
**Merge:** Periodically merge local models to ensure global consistency.
- **Learning Rate Scaling:** The learning rate is scaled by the square root of the batch size.
- **OOM on Preload:** Setting `--preload_dataset_to_gpu` on large datasets can cause Out-Of-Memory errors.
- **Load Balancing:** Uneven distribution of scene complexity or camera views can lead to load imbalance.
- **Time Complexity:** Scales with the number of nodes and Gaussians.
- On Richtmyer-Meshkov dataset (106.7M Gaussians, 5.3 GB, 2048x2048): 3.1x speedup from 4 to 8 nodes.
- **When to Use:** Large-scale scenes (e.g., scientific volumes, high-res urban scans) that exceed single-GPU memory.
- **When Not to Use:** Small to moderate scenes where single-GPU training is sufficient and faster due to lower communication overhead.
